key_insight: Neu-PiG introduces a neural preconditioned latent-grid encoding that enables orders-of-magnitude faster deformation optimization for temporally consistent surface reconstruction, making long unstructured point-cloud sequences tractable without category-specific training.
problem_solved: The method addresses slow, drift-prone reconstruction of dynamic 3D surfaces from unstructured point clouds over very long sequences—avoiding incremental drift and heavy per-category learned models.
method: Preconditioned latent-grid encoding: distribute spatial features on a latent grid to represent geometry compactly and locally.
Neural preconditioner + fast optimization: use learned preconditioning to accelerate iterative deformation optimization and stabilize temporal consistency.
Generalizable pipeline for unstructured point clouds: efficient, non-category-specific reconstruction that scales to long sequences with reduced runtime and drift.
impact: Neu-PiG enables practitioners to reconstruct long, dynamic 3D sequences far faster and with fewer artifacts, lowering compute/time barriers for applications in motion capture, AR/VR, and 3D scanning workflows.
visual_elements: Diagram of the latent grid showing distributed spatial features and how the neural preconditioner interacts with optimization steps.

paper_title: Neu-PiG: Neural Preconditioned Grids for Fast Dynamic Surface Reconstruction on Long Sequences
paper_authors: Julian Kaltheuner, Hannah Dröge, Markus Plack, Patrick Stotko, Reinhard Klein
